mechanism.description: Tectonic's internal TONIC/USD price feed on Cronos: an AggregatorV3-shaped contract with 12 decimals whose only setter, updatePrice(roundId, timestamp, price), is owner-only. The owner is a Multicall3-shaped contract; one externally owned account calls its aggregate3 with updatePrice for 23 or 24 Tectonic feeds per transaction, about every 29 minutes. The contract has no getter for a deviation bound, a minimum or maximum answer, or a minimum interval, and no maximum age: nothing on chain checks the posted value. Class B, posted without guard. The 2026-08-30 exploit blocks were discarded by the chain rollback; on the canonical chain the feed shows ordinary posts, then 26.5 hours of silence.

source.path: selector scan of the deployed bytecode (17 selectors, resolved on openchain) and Tectonic's Price Oracle docs page
source.note: chain reads by the research teammate on 2026-09-01 (raw/cronos-tonic-oracle-chain-reads-2026-09-01.md, wiki/cronos-incident-2026.md). The source is not verified; the selector scan is the evidence for the single setter and the absent guard getters. No explorer API serves Cronos to this tool (cronos.org/explorer 404, Cronoscan 502, explorer-api.cronos.org keyed) and both public RPCs prune state, so explorer is null, rounds come from eth_getLogs in 2,000-block windows from logs.start_block (2026-08-29; round ids are the position in that window), getters are read at a recent block, and no transaction list exists: failed setter attempts are not observable. The contract emits the round id as a millisecond timestamp; it is kept as the field round_id_ms.

relays.note: the oracle's owner contract; Multicall3.aggregate3((address,bool,bytes)[]) carrying updatePrice for 23 or 24 Tectonic feeds, the element targeting this feed is the posting call
